title: How slow should a big plant's clock be?
question: Three of these four cost the SAME speed. Which box do you want to play in? (And if it is the top one, say so — that is the slow one and worth knowing you want it.)
context_md:
You asked for a gallery with the plants given room, so this is a wider bed — 1024 across, 6 founders — at 40,000 frames. Each tree is its own, not a merged canopy.

**The headline is that steepness has stopped buying speed.** A plant waiting longer between ticks the bigger it gets is worth a lot the first time (2.6x -> 5.2x). Pushing it further does exactly what it should to the plant work — that pass keeps halving, 0.445 -> 0.331 -> 0.226 ms — but the frame barely moves, because on a box this wide the CA sweep (1.4 ms) and the field (1.4 ms) dominate and neither cares how often a plant ticks.

So among the bottom three, **you are choosing a look, not a speed.**

**Why this bed and not the one I measured before.** On a 512-wide box the plant pass is 43% of the frame and the steep setting was worth 1.7x. Here it is 14% and worth nothing. Same lever, same effect, different denominator — the sweep and field scale with the *area* of the box, the plants do not. If you mostly play a big box, plant cadence is close to spent and the sweep is the next target.

**What to ignore:** the exact tree count. These are one seed each; the ten-seed sweep comes after you pick, not before.

**What I am unsure of:** whether the sparser boxes read as a healthy stand or as a box that lost its undergrowth. The counts say more leaf per plant and the same biomass, but I cannot tell you whether it *looks* like a wood.

items.label: A — every plant on the same clock (2.6x)
items.caption: current engine default; the slow one

items.label: B — gentle: a grown tree waits 5x (5.2x)
items.caption: what the lab ships today

items.label: C — middle: a grown tree waits 10x (5.5x)
items.caption: same speed as B, fewer and larger plants

items.label: D — steep: a grown tree waits 16x (5.3x)
items.caption: same speed again, fewest plants
